I honestly don't think I've played the game enough to justify if this is truly a great game but here are all my thoughts anyway...

I personally think this game is quite entertaining because I find mowing lawns (with a riding tractor) fun and enjoyable and sometimes feel like I haven't done enough. But this game is far more than mowing a lawn. Let's put down a list of great activities you can do in this game, some of which you can do in previous games too ie FS 15 and FS 13.

1. Running a crop farm. Basically means you take out your planting machines (sowing machines, not to be confused with sewing) and cover a field in crops of variation, wait, then take out the according harvesting combine to pick it up and sell the collected crop.

2. Mowing lawns. Yes if you really wanted, you can waste time mowing lawns, collecting grass and selling it OR using it to feed your animals to make a good profit.

3. Wood cutting. You can take out whats called a "Dangle Head" tree cutter that will cut down and cut up a tree into logs to fit onto a wood trailer to transport them to a log cutting facility, or alternatively you can crunch up the logs into chips and sell them at the heating plant.

4. Taking care of animals. This comes down from #2 where you can take care of cows, sheep, or pigs in order to produce manure from pigs and cows to help with #1. Sheep only take water and grass in order to produce wool which can be transported to a spinnery for good profit. Cows are a bit more difficult but quite rewarding in the long run but are fed a mixture of silage, grass, and straw along with water. Pigs, to be honest, I don't mess with them only because I don't feel the need, but theres a whole guide explaining what you need to do with caring for animals.

If you don't really find much of that appealling then lets go over some features that were added since FS 15.

1. Built in Mod Hub. Yes this game offers a built in mod menu with a ton of mods made by the community.

2. Free dumping of crops or seed or whatever. This means that if you got a trailer full of lets say, wheat, you can dump it pretty much where ever you want and pick it back up later, this applies to all things that can be put in a tipper.

3. Enhanced graphics. I know that the graphics in most cases aren't that much different from FS 15 but there is a noticable improvement that makes the game feel more alive. Plus better attention to detail when it comes to the tractors and equipment.

4. More tractors and equipment such as Fendt, Challenger, and Massey Ferguson. And larger equipment such as the Amazone Condor sowing machine that has a massive span of 15m compared to earlier games such as FS 15 with the Horsche Pronto sower being the biggest in that game with having a span of only 9m.

In conclusion, I think this game is great if you are looking to relax and learn a little bit on certain activities played by real farmers around the world. Theres a ton more features that I can think of but would just make this review too long if I go more.

Over a 1000 hours spent on this, many of them making my Broxton map,  and I've now spent a couple of hundred hours farming it. 
People might be inclined to mock players of this game, for some reason it might draw the same kind of ridicule as a train sim (nothing wrong with them either). But I don't care about that - It's a great fun game/arcade sim with plenty to do, and loads of mods - tractors and implements of all ages and maps to suit all tastes. 
I worked on a farm in the Broxton area many years ago, and this game really takes me back to the feel of real farming. The graphic models of Giants' tractors and all equipment are superb, so mods are not essential, but the many mods on offer definitely add to the game.
The default game is a bit simplified, so it can appeal to all ages, but still it is good enough to feel like some real farming, and if you want more realism, there are plenty of third party mods that increase the realism, Seasons being the first one that comes to mind.
If you're tired of/not a fan of fast paced shooters, and want a more relaxed challenge, then this is a great change of pace.
Recommended.

Need to wind down after a hard days work? This is the game for you. Just sit back and relax. Nobody is trying to kill you and you are not trying to kill anyone.  It's just you, your animals, tractors, and awesome equipment that you had no idea existed.  I have learned an awful lot about the agriculture busniness. Just because of this game I was searching google for how farmers do this in real life and to my surprise the equipement, precision, and science is immence. This game does have a large learning curve and it does not hold your hand. You are free to do whatever you want with little to no consequences.  Now here's the thing.  99% of the player base do not play vanilla. They're using community created mods and maps.  The FS community has created brilliant mods that can make the game more realistic and challenging if you so wish or plough with the same tractor your grandpa had when you were a kid. Oh the nastalga and memories. GIANTS has made a game that people can easily get into, but that's where it falls short. It's not a simulator and it is not realistic at all.

VANILLA FARMING SIMULATOR 17

No Seasons
No Breakdowns or Repairs
No Damage Simulations
No Bankruptcy - infinite negative bank balance
No weeds
No crop destruction if you drive through a germinating field.
No pests
No animal diseases or deaths
No Drought
No Floods
Straw, Hay, and Grass do not rot
Fields are flat.
Perfect Square fields
Tracters drive like they're on asphalt. Even in a bumpy muddy and ploughed field.
Your tires don't even get dirty like they should.
Terrible AI that only works in a straight line, which is why the fields are either square or rectangular.
Crappy phyiscs engine, which makes manual pallet and bale work tedious.
You're the ghost in the town and people don't notice you
Traffic gets in your way and won't move. They just honk their horn in anger. So you save, exit, reload your save and turn traffic off. The annoyance is gone. Now it's a ghost town.

MODDED FARMING SIMULATOR 17

Seasons Mod - Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter - You must plan and develope your farm to prepare for the coming seasons, weather forcast, and animals, which will die if you don't take care of them.  Geological weather data. Perform regular maintanence on your vehichles or inpede a high penalty cost. Snow, rain, hail and crops will die if planted in the wrong seasons and they won't even germinate if the soil tempture is too low.

GPS Mod - Sophisticated GPS System, which the real modern tractors have. The tractor will lock the front wheels to the coordinates of the hud. It's a really good option to use if you want to do a neat and tidy job yourself.

CoursePlay 5 - AI actually works in all field shapes. Not just squares and rectangles. You can completely automate your farm when it becomes too large for a one man team. There's even a handy manual online.

AutoCombine - Similar to courseplay, but only works for field work. Courseplay is better.

Crop Destruction - you can no longer drive though your crops without destorying them.

Ground Response - Your tractor is no longer driving on asphalt, but a ploughed bumpy field.

Drive Control - Oh? Your tractor is slipping now because of the ground response? Use this for 4WD and differential locks.

Tire Dirt - Your tires actually get dirty in the field.

ProSeed - Creates tram lines, which prevents your tires from destorying the crop and it works well with crop destruction mod and you can even turn off 1/2 of the seeder to make sure the tram lines are perfectly placed down withthe same width of your fertlizer spreader or sprayor, just like they do in real life.

Tons of high quality tractors to choose from. 
- FS15 No Fendt. MODS Fendt's galore. John Deere.
- FS17 Fendt. MODS John Deere. I especially love the R7 mod by TM. I seem to recall a tweet from GIANTS about acquiring the rights for John Deere tractors for FS19.

The physics eh? Hard to put pallets and bales on your trailer? It's the engines fault. Install the mod that improves it, albeit only marginally, or just use a trailer with an Autoload script that will put all the bales and pallets perfectly stacked and alligned on the trailer for you. 1 hour job done in seconds!

Add more crop types. Apple orchard, oranges, cherries etc. 

Most importantly. Waaaaaayy better maps!! Sandy Bay17, Chellington, The West Coast, Churn! Challenging terrain and field shapes. Bah just try and use GIANTS AI with those fields.

Add more animals. - which reminds me
- FS15 Chickens, Sheep, Cows ---> MOD Pigs and slaughter houses.
- FS17 Chickens, Sheep, Cows, Pigs. Sell your cows and pigs ---> MOD Horses
- Confirmed FS19 Chickens, Sheep, Cows, Pigs, Horses ---> MOD Pikachu?  I'd like to care for a pikachu.

You can go on Youtube for tutorials on these mods. It's very easy.

GIANTS is outsourcing talent from across the world and paying the mod authors for every download their mod gets.  Your mod will only be entered into the ModHub after it passes the lengthy testing phase by GIANTS and it must be rated 4 stars or more by the user base in order to get paid.  Soybeans and Sugarcane? You could add those crops, tools, and equipment to harvest it before with a mod in FS15 and now its here officially in 17. This is what GIANTS and other big name software companies, like Bethesda, are doing.  Since the mod community does their job for them? There is next to no innovation each release to GIANTS Editor and their game engine since 2007. What kind of improvements should we expect for FS19?

"High Dynamic Range Rendering allows us to display the complete spectrum of colors at the same time, the added Bloom will make light irradiation much more realistic, thanks to SSAO all objects in the game now cast their own shadows, which will be realistically cast thanks to the new Light Scattering technique. The sun on the new dynamic sky now serves as a light source and the clouds, which are now voxel-based 3D objects, reflect the light absolutely realistically."

 Oh. Eye candy and fluff. HDR, which is a 1984 technique they can do on their lunch break and SSAO, which was developed in 2007 by Crytek. Litterly nothing we have seen before, but it is an improvement to their engine. It really shows how behind and old their engine is in a niche market. I'm tired of the 2D field textures, since 2007, that try real hard to look 3D. I'll be waiting till a mod author comes up with that idea.

This game has everything for every type of player. I myself play more on the realism side and add all the realistic enhancing mods like Seasons, which changes the base game drastically to the point it's not the same game anymore that GIANTS envisioned. Remember that when you read these reviews and keep downloading these mods to support the mod authors.

A focus that I'll put on my comments here is that there is the ability to perform work on other farmers fields. Having put a nice chunk of time into FS 2013 back in the year 2012, I had spent a lot of time performing chores, then setting the clock to run at 120x speed, while I waited to perform a harvest. Eventually I could diversify the operation which could keep me busy longer, but it took a very long time to accumulate the equipment necessary.

In 2017, money is very easy to acquire by performing work on other farmers fields. So far I've put about 18+ hours into the game and I've already accumulated well over $300,000 in the first day of “game time”. 

There's so much money to be made doing this that while there are reasons why I would want to advance time, such as accumulating a couple harvests to have enough food to get into animal tending, I don't feel the need to.

By being able to pull in significant chunks of money fairly quickly, I am now quickly planning how I can get into logging and purchasing bigger fields alongside my plans for tending to animals. In 2013, it was a long slog to get new machines that would make things a bit easier. I'm sure some people exploited things or used cheats to make cash fast, but I wasn't on board with doing that myself.
Overall I feel that the mission design allows the player to put time into the game and get easily apparent rewards that facilitates the player's quest to become more deeply acquainted with the various features of the game.

Besides that, there have been huge upgrades to the graphics since 2013, which is to be expected but casual fans like myself who got on the FS train back in 2012 will be pleased with the new details and animations. Zooming in on various machines while they work is a treat, with soil being deformed and pushed aside, or corn rows being drawn into a corn harvest header. I also really like how machines get dirty and can even be cleaned by cleaning equipment that is operated by the player. Even the interior cabins of machines will have dirty boot prints as you get in and out of them with dirty boots. 

Controls wise, I've used KB+Mouse and found them to be great. I am currently using an Xbox 360 controller while sitting on the couch using a TV instead of my monitor and it's even more enjoyable. I have a G27 steering wheel setup but I enjoy sitting back on the couch with this game so I don't feel the need to deepen the simulation with that controller setup. I'm glad that it supports that hardware if I feel so inclined in the future though!

Overall, I find that these games really offer a deep experience of getting to know your farms, your equipment and building a farming empire. The tutorials are very easy to understand (I didn't need most of them but I did some of them anyway) and I liked how they easily allowed me to perform the steps with the game's equipment so I could see what type of hardware I might buy and how I would use it for my in-game farm when I'm ready. New players shouldn't have too much trouble if they have free time and some interest. I find it's really neat to get involved with the farming simulator world, much more immersion than a lot of the shooters and other games which offer transient game experiences.

I haven't tried multiplayer but it's a welcome addition. From viewing YouTube videos it really appears to be a great way to play and something you might really enjoy. I personally like coming home from work and loading up the farm and getting some stuff done whenever I want; without having to coordinate with friends. So MP is less of a thing for me, but once again, a welcome feature.

I tend to marvel at little things in the game, like using a front-end loader to pick up bales or using a shovel to scrape up a pile of something off of the ground. The fact that the game simulates piles of materials is neat. Although I find it slightly bothersome that I can't shift in my seat while using the virtual cockpits; it would be nice to shift around and see different angles while seated. That would help operate multiple different types of machines. Although being able to look around the cockpit is nice enough and popping in and out of third person isn't a problem anyway.

This game really is a deep experience that rewards the player and gives a sense of satisfaction that most games can't. It's also nice to play a game where the world is at peace and one's only worries is how will they spend their day at their beautiful farm.

TL;DR: The best farming simulator out today.

[h1] Review [/h1]

If you like Simulation games, this is a great one to add to your collection. It's a great family and cooperative game that is both fairly relaxing and deceptively challenging. You can certainly play the game casually, but playing it as intended means a fair dedication of time. It will take a long time to do everything there is to do, and there is a lot of it. Farming ranges from the typical grains to the more involved root crops. You also have animal husbandry available and it goes well when done side-by-side with regular farming. The last major job available is Forestry, which is one of the most engaging tasks available in the game, although it can be frustrating due to in-game physics.

Each map starts you with a couple of fields, farming equipment, and a loan of varying amounts depending on the difficulty. From there on, you make your decisions as to how to play and what to do. You can sell all your equipment right from the start and do whatever you like. Fields you don't yet own are "owned" by NPCs who will offer you jobs to work that field and is a great way to make early money. Just don't spend too much time on other fields and not your own. Each job raises your reputation for that field and in turn lowers the price to purchase. Jobs are unfortunately but understandably not available in multiplayer. You can take a bigger loan to expand your business, make money from selling crops when the price is high, or even hunt hidden "nuggets" for a big cash bonus and an achievement. 

The amount of vehicles and tools available to help you in your chosen roles is astounding and here might be one of the drawbacks. It can take a while to fully understand what they all do and what the advantages of each are. You are likely to have a whole selection of these that you will just never use unless you purposely try them all. With more tools and attachments come more key bindings to remember. The F1 help menu is great at listing the main keyboard shorcuts, but many are only learned if you dig deep. The game is not difficult to play by any means, but it is difficult to master. Parents who play with their kids should definitely aim for about 6-7 yrs and up unless your child is very familiar with these type of games.

Graphics are great for what the game is looking to achieve. Most of the game engine power will be dedicated to tracking your crop and equipment status and you'll grow to have a lot. The equipment is incredibly detailed with great animations of moving parts all realistically working. Older computers can still play the game but will be forced to lower settings and limit the amount of equipment on the screen. Forestry may be very difficult with slower PCs as the tree rendering and physics will cause lag. Sound design is decent but some of the machines do not feel powerful. Sounds are also shared across some equipment which leaves little to tell them apart sound-wise. I imagine some of these tractors and harvesters have very unique engine notes that sadly do not stand out. There is a built-in game radio that your can tune to online music streams and comes with some basic "radio stations" with a few songs each. You'll likely listen to your favorite music separately and never use the in-game offerings.

If you like downloading add-ons or "mods" for games, you will find a wealthy offering by the community. The game features a built-in mod browsers which is a huge step up over previous versions. The mods available here pale in comparison to those available at many online sites, however. Do be warned that some of these sites may have ads or even malware, so be careful when browsing. The community mods can vastly add and transform the game, making it more realistic, larger, adding more vehicles, crops and even jobs like mining. Giants also has DLC avaliable, but nothing that you really need. Kuhn DLC has extra tools but nothing spectacular except the square bale wrapper. The Big Bud DLC requires a large map and you won't have the need for big tractors unless you're later in the game and made some money for bigger fields.

All in all there is a lot to do here. If a job gets too boring there are other ways to do it or other jobs to do to keep it different. There's multiple approaches to almost all jobs and money making is fairly balanced if you're playing it as designed, so just do what you like. You'll obviously have to like the sim genre, but the game offer the best farming simulation out there. With several major releases under their belt, this latest release really does have a complete package. Not entirely without faults, but it is by far the best of its type out there, and a fantastic investment in terms of play value; especially with friends. Highly Recommended. 

If you are unsure about whether you would like the game, or cannot afford it, you will find a lot of what FS17 has to offer in the older FS15, but the newer version is definitely superior. See these notes below for some of the differences

[h1] Notes for owners of Farm Sim 2013/2015 [/h1]

If you own the older FS13, you will find a huge step up in content. There are changes to some mechanics so watch a couple of videos online if you're not too sure. Definitely worth the upgrade.

FS15 players I know are going to be on the fence. I actually decided to write this review almost just to point out some of the reasons to upgrade. Obviously this will be personal opinion but I feel those saying FS17 offers nothing new from 15 are wrong. Here is is a quick list of the new things:

[list]
[*]Soybeans and sunflowers now stock crops
[*]Pig farming
[*]New vehicle types like weeders (Work like fertilizer)
[*]Performance improvements (FS17 runs better and looks better on my PC over FS15)
[*]In-game Mod hub
[*]You can pickup and move objects (Great for Forest work in a budget)
[*]You can strap objects down! (No more logs floping all over during transport)
[*]Vehicle customization (Change engines wheels and other options in the shop, you can upgrade vehicles after purchase)
[*]Vehicle lease/rent now stock
[*]3 Fertilizing stages + plowing actually does something (+10 % yield from plowing)
[/list]

Catch it on a sale if you want, but it is worth the update to FS17. FS15 mods are almost all available in 17, and the new Platinum version coming out in November actually looks pretty good. Adds sugarcane farming!

[h1]Summary[/h1]

If you're a farming fan - this is the real deal - surely the best simulator of this kind on the market. It is well worth its prize and if you own Farming Simulator 15, just like I do, changes really justify buying it. I can heartily recommend it. 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
1. High-end graphics that are very stable and not demanding.
2. Enough machines and equipment to make your head spin, and what's more, most of them are further customizable, and even more - there are countless mods available directly from the game's menu.
3. Three kinds of animals for you to buy, transport, and feed, each with their own requirements. Also - chicken that require nothing and still provide you with fresh eggs to sell in the town. 
4. There is a fully simulated train for you to use and drive around.
5. Maps are pretty nice and immersive. 
6. Missions for other farmers where you have to help them with different tasks is a nice touch and a great way to end some additional money in the early game.
7. There is an in-game radio, although I still prefer my own collection of John Denver.
8. There are many options to customize your experience, mainly game's difficulty. Mods provide additional options. 

[h1]Cons[/h1]
1. Physics can be hilarious.
2. Your helpers get stuck way too easily, and when getting around the obstacle is no brainer at all. 
3. There are very few AI cars driving around and drivers are morons.

It's Nov 2020 and Farming Simulator 2017 is still on my PC. 

I'm 100's of hours in at this point in time and still happy I stuck to the title.

A note about FS2019
I need to be clear, I have no problem with FS2019. I didn't get FS2019 for the same reason as I didn't get FS2015 when I was playing FS2013 ... every two years a new edition drops, which, eventhough it does build on the last, doesn't always represent value for money for me. I personally treat it as a sim and as such, it take times for me to get the setup I want, find the mods I prefer, make the edits I wish to have. Then to get on with enjoying the experience I've eventually built only for a new title to drop soon after and I have to start all over again is not what I need. The second edition down the line usually packs good bang for buck, builds on it's predecessor and represents a worthwhile purchase.
So the skipped 2019 which worked for me so far.

If you are new to Farming Simulator and happen to be reading this review, (unlikely I know)  I would recommend you look at FS2019. It is the better entry point and the community have already had plently of time to build up the mod databases also.

All that said, FS2017 is still an active and enjoyable FS edition and one which I can also recommend if for some reason, FS2019 is no an option for you. You can see by the price it commands also that it's popular. 

The mod community has been very active and for those with FS2017 already, it's so good that  I personally see little reason to move on.

A future expected Farming Simulator 2021 is confirmed by Giants as not happening (at least against the expected 2-year schedule (Sept)  that the previous many editions released on).

1) Lately I've been really keen on games that let you customize and open - world decisions.  Games that you aren't restricted to a set path.  I bought FS17 on a whim when it was on sale and fell in love with it - to my own surprise.

2) I've always been a community organizer and so knew that this game is far better when played with other people.  Sure I'm a nerd because I game so much, and play D&D, but it blew me away how much I enjoyed FS17.  Not something I ever thought I'd like.  I think what pulled me in is the fact that it isn't scripted.  There is no "What should i do next" hand holding.  It's an open-ended relaxing game where you get to drive big awesome machines.  At my prime I was spending every evening playing FS17 when running the server for several hours.  When the server was very popular I would easily spend 3-4 hours a night playing.  Much longer on the weekends.

3) Our server was a little more relaxed then other multiplayer servers.  We aimed to have a "community" as opposed to a "simulation" of farming.  We recognized we were all gamers.  We would have community events in game and invite everyone to join.  Everyone took a round of shots while we drove trucks around town doing deliveries.  Any time someone crashed we wouldn't "reset" the vehicles, we had to go get tow bars and pull them out.  Made for lots of laughs.  We switched maps 4-5 times during the time I hosted the server.  Each map filled a different need and made by excellent map makers in the community like Stevie and Dajnet.  Most recently we were on Pleasant Valley v3.1, a map by Dajnet.  It is an amazing map and allowed us to support several more players on our server as the map alone has 6 different standalone farms.

The only thing I noticed with this game as opposed to other communities I've created in other games is the turnover rate is very high.  People don't stick around FS17 as much as other communities.  They get anxious to try new maps, or other games, or play more casually.  Not as many 'gamers' play FS17 but there were a handful.

4) Recommended to be heavily modded.  The vanilla version of the game is not designed very well when it comes to multiplayer.  The game really comes alive and fun when you start installing mods.  Very unique maps with new machines, new equipment and tractors, new manufacturing features.  The vanilla game gets repetitive and boring very quickly.  But Mods make it a much better experience with thousands of activities to do, depending on your combination of maps and mods.

In addition, I played for several months with mouse and Keyboard but the game felt new again after I purchased a Wheel, pedals, and a Joystick.

5)Other servers that are legitimately organized seem to be a lot different.  Everyone has an opinion when they transfer from an old server, "my server used to do it this way...".  So there is a lot of variation.  Some servers don't care about realism so they will mod their machines to go ridiculously fast, or hold way too much materials.  Other servers have TOO MUCH realism in my opinion, and don't allow players to drive anywhere but on the roads with certain vehicles.  We were somewhere in between.  The only thing I wish Giants would improve would be their multiplayer features.  It was really difficult to keep an ongoing server going with limited access to how in game funds work.  Lots of mods helped fix this. 

As a result, I know several servers even ran the game with a bunch of spreadsheets, and tracked their expenses out of game.  I did that for too long in EVE online that when I switched to FS17 I wanted a much more casual experience.  So we made it work on our server with mods, even though it wasn't perfect.

A great gaming experience all around, and will appeal to gamers that least expect it.

I was curious about this game for years and finally took the plunge since it was on sale. It was well worth the ten dollars. There's a lot of things to do epecially if you add mods. You can play the game several different ways. If you're the kind of person that likes to grind to get better equipment and nicer stuff, the vanilla game is perfect for you. Each and every upgrade will feel extremely rewarding because you worked for it. If you're the type that wants the best equipment quickly, you can do that too by building up enough money to buy things like solar panels which earn income and require no maintanence. To get money quickly you can exploit the game by speeding up time and buying more solar panels from the income until you eventually can buy wind turbines which make lots of money. You could literally turn your farm into a wind farm and be a billionaire and buy everything you want and do it rather quickly. It's certainly not challenging and the sense of reward will be gone, but the option is there for people who just want to buy and collect everything. You can also try to find 100 hidden gold nuggets which is fun and challenging and has a huge monetary payback. This feels much more rewarding because it takes time and work. You can raise animals which can become very involved but is quite fun if you like to keep busy. You must grow or buy ingredients for their feed, mix their feed, give them bedding, clean their mess and use it for fertilizer or sell it, breed them, etc. You can log forests and if you download the mods you can eventually sell furniture. Or you can just farm your own fields if you like. There is even a map with a quarry that makes concrete and other items as a download. You can download excellent modded maps like Pinecove which has tons of room to expand by placing buildings you purchase. You can produce your own silage in several different ways. There are mods that have antique tractors and farming equipment and maps of old farms you can start on if you want to go old school. There are also giant maps with industry. You can buy property and you can lower the prices of these properties by doing missions. You can do farming missions for other NPC farmers for money using their equipment and make good money. You can store your fruits and grains in silos and wait until demand is high and increase your profit.  Some mods completely change the game "Gifts of the Caucacus" mod has  an airplane you can hire to fertilize your fields while you ride along, A quarry, shops where you can drop off your material and get other material which in turn leads to making items you can sell elsewhere. On this map in order to do forestry you must do a quest involving finding the missing forestry equipment hidden all over the map. On this map you can also purchase factories and shops from a realtor if you raise your reputation and have a lot of cash. Tons of stuff to do! There are sonme drawbacks. Doing missions for other farmers actually pays more than raising your own crops. So if you're only in it for the money, it  spoils the game a bit. You still get a lot of satisfaction of going through all the stages of growing a final product if you farm for yourself, but all that work isn't going to make you the most money. If you're just in it to get the reward of managing a successful farm than the lucrative issues shouldn't be a problem. just do them if you need cash quickly. Maintenance fees are also somewhat of a chore as you'll find yourself selling old equipment because it costs too much too maintain. You can overcome this by purchasing things like solar panels or turbines  to effectively cancel the hassle and even cut a profit. There are small maps and large maps. There are in game mods and third party mods and all of them are easy to install if you've ever modded before or just Youtube them for instructions if you're not mod savvy. This game is a relaxing kind of game. It's a stress reliever....unless you're trying to manage 300 cows, sheep, and pigs....lol!

Let me start off by setting the tone.

I've played since FS11 and despite the radical inclusion of forestry in FS15, which I enjoyed very much, I was still very bitter towards GIANTS and their progress from 11 to 15. I felt their added features lacking, their improvements lacking and overall vision or direction absent. Their DLCs quite often were obvious money grabs, rather than any real addition to a player's farming strategy. 

Odds are, they were a small but up and coming software development team which accomplished what they could, considering they were also creating smaller versions of the game for the Android and iOS platforms. Maybe they were spread too thin.

This year, they release FS17 with a $45 price tag, up from $29 in the past and I couldn't help but facepalm myself. I sarcastically thought, "Let me guess, we'll have MORE TRACTORS" as a way to justify the new cost.

24 literal gameplay hours into it, and I have to say, it has caught up to most of my expectations. Kudos for bringing this game up to speed and making it almost worth the $45. It's about time. 

The game mechanics haven't changed a whole lot. It seems like midway through FS15, before they fleshed out all the bugs, they cloned it and started making FS17. This would explain a lot of the bugs that were resolved late in FS15 showing up in FS17. Currently, the "jitter bug" prevents me from doing forestry unless I use autoload trailer mods. 

So what's the deal?

Missions have changed. Previously we had delivery and mowing missions. I didn't mind the delivery ones, but they were sorta boring. The mowing missions I enjoyed. They're now gone, which I don't think is right. They should come back and with more variety. 

Now, we have missions where we are maintaining other farmer's fields. Thing is, you can't hire anyone to do it. You have to do it yourself. I would prefer to be able to hire, even if it meant it would cut into my profit.

There are a few more crops, 1 more live stock (pigs), chickens haven't changed and lots of tractors. There are even two useless trains. Well, useless on the Goldcrest Valley map. Two little loops around the center of the map. Regardless, it will make for great maps by the modders. Goldcrest Valley is an awful map. How is it that modders make better maps?

Despite my gripes... I'm really addicted to this game.

And with the $45 price tag and $19 DLCs... they'd better be making a phenomenal FS2019.

If you liked Farming Simulator 15, 17 is worth the cost.

This game can seem overwhelming at first to someone who has never played a Farming Sim before, and knows nothing about farming. It is challenging to the newcomer like me, but if you invest in the tutorials and help menus, you will learn as you go and enjoy it. However, I am very addicted so far and I will list below why:

Side note: There are some tutorials out there on how to make tons of money right off the bat with the game. Usually it involves selling everything you own, maxing out your loan, and installing solar panels, then leaving your system on for 3 solid real time days......I recommend not doing that, as IF you follow the basics of the game, such as farming multiple crop types, fertilizing, and only selling harvests when prices are high, you will make plenty of money and it will be YOUR hard earned work and rewards, not an exploit. 

Here's what I like about the game:
- Multiple ways to make money, farming numerous types of crop, harvesting lumber, working other farmers fields for really good pay, installing money generating placeables on your farm, etc.
 
- Very technical game with attention to detail and the graphics and modelling matches that. If you do not like simulation games or have some hatred of farmers, then you won't like this game.

- Steep learning curve but not overwhelming, just follow the tutorials and help menus, and work your way up to new crops and new machines.

- The financial system is fairly simple yet robust, and really does well to make you feel like YOU OWN each piece of equipment with your hard work and savings. You have a list of various buyers for your crops, that list is color coded to prices (demand) that are bad, neutral, good, and really good (high demand). You can borrow up to $300K in loans, which do not have any time limit to pay them back, but you are charged interest each day until you do. 

-This game runs VERY well even on full graphics. The graphics are very good, and the game runs super smooth even though I have an older gaming PC. 

- I have not yet found any glitches or bugs, again it runs smooth. 

- A LOT of control over your difficulty. You can choose Easy Medium or Hard as usual, but you get further control over, how often you have to fertilize crops, whether or not your crops whither and so on. This tweaking really lets you play to your play style and skill level (aka, I'm a noob).

- There's a lot more to do than "just farming" you can purchase forklifts, logging equipment, semi-trucks/trailers, and A TON more. This game is packed with A LOT of really cool vehicles that make your life easier and give you variety in what to do.  

- I like that you can hire AI helpers (good AI with a few hiccups) to take over various time consuming tasks while you do other stuff. Using them properly is the absolute key to success when farming by yourself in a time efficient manner. 

- You have hands on control of your farming output from start to finish. I love the fact that you decide what crops go in what field, you put work into increasing the yield of those crops, harvesting those crops, storing those crops in your silos, and eventually loading up those crops into a trailer and hauling them with your pickup to sell to a vendor. From start to finish you get to be involved in it all, or have AI workers help where needed. 

- MOD SUPPORT!

- You get hundreds of hours of game-play from a game that costs $35 full retail. 

Things I don't like:
- The more your vehicles/equipment age, the more they cost per day to keep, I feel this happens a bit too fast. This is deducted from you at midnight of each day, going into the thousands per day or more. There is no way to remedy this other than selling off the old rig (for next to nothing) and purchasing a new one (which could be A LOT of money). This really cuts into your bottom dollar, but is also realistic in managing your overall farm. So it's a positive if you like realism, but a steep learning curve for new players.

- The store, which you purchase all of your equipment and supplies, is REALLY far from your farm, making trips there to pick up a new header for your combine (which travels 14 MPH) a real chore. I would have liked to see this store closer. You can however purchase trailers and such to transport pallets of fertilizer and seeds that you buy, and that's fun. You can fast travel to this store by your self (no vehicle with you), but if you need a vehicle to pick up your purchase, you have to drive that vehicle over there and back again, which sucks if it goes 14 mph....

- The controls on the faster vehicles such as your pickup, are quite unrealistic and if you're going fast, it's really easy to spin out. However it is manageable and once you get the hang of it it's not a big deal. 

Overall, this game is really fun, I recommend it to anyone who is open minded about their games, who likes technical/simulation games, or who enjoys management type games where you have a lot of investment into what you own in the game and how well your business does. I feel that Farming Simulator 2017 does this very well, it makes you put stock into the game and feel like you have ownership over your success and the things you own.

Not even sure where to start man.  I got this game because I'm a sim player and the graphics looked nice, and it was on sale.  I'm in LA, so the last thing going on around me is farming, unless you're farming weed.  This game, and it's modders, BLEW MY MIND. 

You do the first two tutorials to get the gist of the controls and the basics of farming.   And it's the basics, I'm 140+ hours in and all I've done is work the fields on the first map.  No animals, I cut down a half dozen trees by chainsaw around my silos that were pissing me off because I kept ramming them, no chaff, hay, manure, blah blah blah, just joyously working the fields, learning where everything is, and buying shit (the lower three fields and better equipment so far).  To say this game is addicting, even to a city dude with zero ties or previous interest in farming, is a gross understatement.  Just playing the basics, you realize the layers of this game just go on and on, and how each crop (and animals when you get them)  interweaves with different functions of your farm, and each other, is one of the coolest applications of resource management I've seen, and I've got probably 50 RM games.

So the playability alone is endlessly challenging and engaging, but then you start adding the insane amounts of equipment that these farmers really use because certain crops need certain specialty equipment, fields of different sizes and shapes (not all of which can be worked completely with hired help), different crop cycles and crops, seasons if you want them.  It just doesn't end.

Then there's a second map to do it all over again.  Two maps normally draw a smirk from people, but all it takes is the two tutorials and 30 minutes on the first map, and you know you're in for some serious simming.

Then we go to the modding community.  I play (for better or for worse) many of the Paradox titles and their modding communities get pretty crazy in terms of tonnage and quality.  Nah, kiddie pool.  This group of modders, and I'm talking directly to all of you, are THE BEST.  It's not just such a vast array of equipment in every single category that your head explodes (there a dude modding forks for your Polish forklift for crissake!), it's the quality of the art as well.  You're farming in Poland?  No problem, every manufacturer in Poland has gear in this game from harvesters to tractors; Plows, cultivators and seeders; Tippers, tanks,  vats, spreaders, tumblers, turners, and some wind wheel thing that gathers your cut grass into a frickin line so you can gather it with some other piece of equipment.  Germany?  Sweden?  Italy?  Russia?  Got you covered, and which manufacturer did you want to purchase again?  Just so ridiculous that experienced players must be in hog heaven using all this stuff.  I can't wait to get there.  

That brings me to maps.  I made two sound like enough for this game, and it is.  How about 100 others in all parts of the world in real settings?  Almost all done with the same detail as the devs, but each has new ideas, killer layouts, different sizes, new start points with different field and equipment manifests, and all new crops, animals and functions not even found in the original game.  There are six regular and two root crops in the base game.  I think four animals if you count the chickens.  I've seen some of these maps with 14 crops and 8 animals types.  Then instead of 35 fields or so (you start with owning three), how about 80 and you start with 2 and less equipment?

Want even more play?  Play EVERY SINGLE MAP on one of three difficulty levels and start each game with lower resources, market buying and selling prices, and more difficult game dynamics.  I've got major time invested in a few games on my list and I can already tell this one is going straight to the top.  Just can't stop playing and discovering/learning new layers.  

Two shakin' thumbs up.

Holy crap! I bought FS22, played for a while and decided FS17 is simply way better - vehicle acceleration is better, turning and other handling is better, graphics are better (yes, graphics in '17 at max are better than '22 at max) and how much of a grind '22 is compared to this, this is better for me. I understand some like it different but for me, if I'm thinking of gathering in-game money to buy something I prefer to get it done in a few gaming sessions instead of 12341242134 sessions.

Having played FS15 already for many hours (1000+), i have mixed feelings about FS17. Yes, the developer "optimized" several things, the graphics look better, overall performance is better, Multiplayer is more forgiving. But where there is light there is also darkness. The performance increase (especially in Multiplayer) came at some cost with sync between players. Players don't see the same stuff anymore. For example the AI Traffic. One player sees several vehicles in front of him, while somebody else sees absolutely nothing. Emptying the manure heap at the cow stables updates several minutes (!!!) later in the Menu. This is ridiculous. 

Modding became a pain in the neck. While Giants published the Sourcecode in previous versions, this time they decided to only write a incomplete function description. There was no information at all from Giants about some important changes in the game (like the new storage system). It just was so painful to create new maps. The forums from Giants are there, but no involvement from Giants. Not one answer on how things changed or worked now.

And let's be honest, Giants made some improvements to the underlying engine, but you do notice that it just opened a can of worms at other ends. The engine is so pretty much at its end of life.

It appears though that Giants focused this time much more on the consoles, for PC Players the game is more of a slap in the face. I don't care if the PS4 doesn't support modding the same way a PC does. I don't care about the politics behind Sony's decision. But you get a crippled product because of this. I am a PC Player, so don't take away the ability to mod the living hell out of this game just because the mods wouldn't work on a PS. 

The modding community is slowly on a decline. If you take a look at the main modding site (No, not Modhub from Giants itself, the other one) you will find the 500th version of the standard map "Goldcrest Valley", a tree moved to the side and a "new" map on modhoster. There are tons of converted mods from LS15 which more or less are full of bugs, lots of re-skins etc. All in all just crap. Real innovative mods are missing this time. Shame, but it is a sign of the changed modding support of this game. 

But...it is still fun to play FS17, as long as you figured out how to work around several of the issues.

If Giants does carry on the path with the next version of FS i have to say that the FS17 will be the last version i bought. 

BTW the upcoming CnC is, from what i saw so far, several years behind the FS in the development stage. So don't hold your breath. 

I am not sure how i should rate the game, there are several good aspects (also compared to previous versions) but i can't agree with the path Giants chose this time. I therefore decide to not recommend the game anymore. Hopefully it will change with the next version again.

[h1]Is Farming Simulator 17 just an [i]"overpriced DLC"[/i] for Farming Simulator 15?[/h1] Why don't you decide for yourself from this review. 

[b]New features:[/b]
[list]
[*] New lighting engine which drastically improves game performance, and allows for light reflections. 
[*] Two additional crop types, Soybeans, and Sunflowers, Oilseed radishes are also present as a cover crop. 
[*] Most sowing machines now have the ability to be filled with seed and fertilizer, similar to their real life counterparts. 
[*] Dynamic piles: You can now unload your trailer anywehere you please! 
[*] Conveyers: These allow you to load piles into trailers. 
[*] Weeders: These can be used on any crop in it's first growth stage to increase yield. 
[*] Vehicle customization: You can now customize asthetic, as well as performance details on most vehicles before purchase. 
[*] Many new brands including Challenger, Fendt, and Massey Fergusin. 
[*] Drivable trains: You can now control trains in the game, these can be used to haul crops, and logs to selling points. 
[*] New missions system: While in Single-Player, you can now work fields around you, and be paid for doing so. Additionally, the more work you do for each farmer, the higher your reputation goes, when this is at it's max level, you will be able to purchase the field at a discount. 
[*] Players can now pick up objects by hand (Providing the objects aren't too heavy!) When logging, you can now pick up your cut logs by hand! 
[*] Tie down straps: You can now tie down cargo on trailers! 
[*] Tire pressure simulation: You will now notice your tires deform under pressure (When you fill a water trailer up, for example.)
[*] Dynamic Silage mounds: You will now have to use a silage plow to shape your chaff from a pile into a nice sloping mound before fermenting. 
[*] The Game engine has finally been optimized to provide very smooth performance at all times (provided you have a decent pc, ofcourse.)  
[/list] 

I have only scraped the surface in this list, i am still discovering new features myself. The new vehicle roster is so large that it will take some time to become bored with all of the stock equipment. 

[b]Negatives:[/b]
[list]
[*] Ground Deformation: This feature is still not present in the game. When asked why this feature was still not present in the game, Giants replied [i]"It would have caused to many syncing issues in Multiplayer."[/i]
[/list]

I am aware that the Cons list is rather short, however i really haven't been able to find much to gripe about with this game. So far, i would consider this a worthwhile investment.

-Physics (handling of bales/pallets; masses of equipment; etc.)
-Graphics (addition of Motion Blur, Depth of Field and Ambient Occlusion effects; shaders to be reworked; rain to have impact on textures; dirt mapping to be more real life-like; entire environment textures reworked and colored properly to have more realistic appearance; etc.)
-Gameplay (full seasons cycle; more difficulty options for players seeking maximum realism; horse power and mass to have impact on implements/trailers used; adjusted pricing of animals, equipment and placeables; separately purchasable biogas plant, animal farms, forests; addition of dynamic terrain and vegetation (highly requested); improved Multiplayer synchronization; etc.)
-Equipment and Animals (more youngtimer equipment that would be suitable for smaller to medium sized farms (highly requested); more animals to be added to the game (beef cattle, broilers, turkeys, goats and more); chickens to be purchasable (this was available in FS 13 and 15) and feedable; etc.)

There's a truckload and more things to be mentioned, but that's enough for now.

My personal score for this Farming Sim would be a strong 9 out of 10, developers put a lot of effort into production of this game, became more open with the modding community and also gave modders an opportunity to participate in contests and create official and fully licensed DLC's.

For the next FS I hope to see some new changes and additions, something that was never seen before in any Farming Simulator game.

I played more than my fair share of FS15, and suffice to say, FS17 is a HUGE step up.

PROS:

* Better graphics
* More equipment
* More fruit types
* Goldcrest Valley is a well-crafted map
* A radio
* The ability to drive trains

CONS:

* The train diehard in me has several questions: why are European trains on American soil? And how can they climb such steep grades best reserved for narrow-gauge geared locomotives?
* Simulator Radio has fucking Justin Bieber
* Losing sleep in unavoidable

I highly recommend this game, its obviously not for those who expect a lot to happen in a short space of time, its very repetitive but isn't that the point? Anyway, here are the good and bad points.

GOOD:
Very high attention to detail: The models in this game are very realistic, slightly better than the previous game but still better.

Mod Manager: Although there aren't many mods available on the Mod Manager, there are still enough to make the game noticeably different. I also love how most of the mods are actually by GIANTS and are FREE which is very respectable because if it was any other developer they would have released them as paid DLC.

Radio: There are 4 radio stations, Rock, Pop, Electro and Country even though the songlist isn't that big its still a decent improvement and hopefully in the future the ability to add your own songs or a radio mod.

New Crops and Vehicles: Its awesome to see new crops in Farming Simulator it obviously adds a lot more realism and at the same time, more work to do.

New Maps: Goldcrest Valley and Soznovka. At the moment I have only played on Goldcrest which is a very well laid out map, so I assume Soznovka will be laid out very well too, I just don't like it because it looks very rustic and I prefer modern.

Vehicle modifications: This is my favourite addition by far, the ability to modify your vehicles adds a bit more flexibility to the vehicles you buy, althought not every vehicle can be modified there are still a lot that can.

BAD:
Animal Animations: They aren't really that bad, but they could be a little bit smoother. When the animals walk they sort of judder and the transition from animations are instant but either way they are still not too bad.

No Crop damage: This can be rectified by downloading a mod using the in-game mod manager, but it would be nice to see that little bit of realism added by default, it could even be toggleable.

Maps: There are only 2 maps, although they are very VERY nice maps, itt would be nice to see more maps by the masters at Giants rather than fan-made. I don't know about you, but the game feels more official when you play on a map made by the devs rather than fans.



Well, thats about it, I know I have only played 42.1 hours as of posting this review but thats still a pretty long time in my opinion considering I do play other games too. So again, I highly recommend this game, especially if you have more than one monitor, its really fun to just play this and watch Netflix on another screen, a great way to chill out :D

That being said, any sand box type of game is really what  you make of it and Farming Sim 17 has the tools to do that, including the shear number of mods available.

It turns out I had massively underestimated this game. Truthfully, I only decided to buy it on the recommendation of a family member who's been playing it for some time. But I finally understand what all the hype is about. I get why there are so many raving reviews.

This title has so much to offer. It's not just about driving tractors and harvesting crops. There's a whole economy to manage too, workers to hire, money to make, and new vehicles and equipment to buy and sell. Furthermore, there's a whole plethora of mods available!

The graphics are beautiful and the sounds are awesome, from the birds singing in the trees, to machinery clunking away in the background. The environment has been well thought out, and there's plenty to keep you busy. Like any great game, it's all too easy to loose track of time as you become totally immersed.

There is a lot of stuff to get used to, so don't expect to be making a success of things when you first get started. I highly recommend going through the tutorials! These will be of huge benefit to you when you start the career mode, as you'll quickly discover that you don't start out with all of the equipment that you really need, so you have to either budget for new equipment or make the best of what you DO have for the time being.

The sheer number of controls and functions is a real mindbender, but it all adds to the experience. I did find that the default controls setup was a bit clumsy and frustrating, so I spent a lot of time remapping them to work with my aging Logitech G25. I believe this title can also be played in VR, which is great news to me as an Oculus owner! I haven't tried it yet though. The TrackIR seems to be doing the job well enough on it's own for the time being. Another useful tool in my opinion, since you often need to be looking both ahead and behind your vehicle while working with some of the equipment.

If you have a wheel/pedals, you WILL want to use them with this game. I can't see the likes of an Xbox controller offering anywhere near the level of functionality and fingertip control that you really need. I know people are getting by just fine with a gamepad, but if you have a controller which offers far more buttons and axes, use it.

This review is coming from somebody who owns FS13, 15, and 17. So I'll be presenting my views for both long time players, and those who haven't owned/played farming simulator before.

If you have a real nice computer to run this on, it's almost a work of art- There's detail where you'd least expect it. The gameplay is also wonderful, you have a couple different "routes" you can go when it comes to making money; making the biggest farm you can, handling huge heards of animals, or furiously logging. The game also has a pretty sophisticated economy, which takes a lot of variables into consideration, and also makes you think about how you can maximize your return on investment.

Compared to previous versions of Farming Simulator, it certainly is an improvement in several categories, including visuals, physics, and general game mechanics. Many people do say that it's not much of an improvement compared to Farming Simulator 15, and I partially agree with them. I feel the part that makes it worth the upgrade would be the assortment of new and improved assets- some things in FS15 just felt poorly put together, meanwhile FS17 offers a wide variety of equipment (with lots of extra options too), all of which brings a new or improved experience to the table.

If you own a previous version of FS, I'd suggest watching YouTube videos of FS17 or potentially seeing if a friend can let you play, because my opinion of it being notably better than FS15 may not be the same as your opinion as to how similar it really is, and you can decide for yourself if it really lives up to the hype.
If you've never owned/played Farming Simulator before, and you're interested in it, I highly suggest this game for you, (partly because there's no major advantage to purchasing an older version), as it'll be able to provide you with hours of fun (or screwing around), and there probably won't be another version until around 2019.

I first want to say that I think unless someone has 100 hours or more on a game they shouldnt be allowed to place a review. My honest opinion of FS 17 is good. Graphics are very good to good a little jerky at times. More attention needs to be made to mega farms such as the farms in the United states not all of us want hobbie farms and yes bigger is better. Animals seem to be an after thought real pigs have litters of 8 to 16 not one at a time 50 cows dont have just 1 calf a season. Sheep usualy have twins and more than 1 a season also Chickens multiply worse than rabbits if you let them sit. Some farmers like to grow animals some like to grow crops. The farming crops side of this game is very good although the selling part sucks when you sell a truckload of grain in real life the price does not go down while you dump you get paid the begining price for the whole load. This game still holds up in 2026. I'd love to try FS25 but I'm having so much fun with this version that I'm in no hurry. You could pick up this game on a sale for less than $5. There was a fix that I had to use to fix a common problem that kept the game from loading and I'll include it below. Once the game loads you'll have countless hours of work ahead of you. the graphics are pretty good for a game from 2017 and the radio plays catchy tunes. After 40 or so hours I started playing my own music in the background because there aren't enough songs in game to keep you from getting bored but you can easily tweak your settings so it's pretty seamless. The only difference is that the music keeps playing after you exit a vehicle. There are endless angles to approach your farming adventure and tons of video's on Youtube to help you on your way. This game is well worth the sale price and more fun than I could have ever expected. Maybe I'm just getting old.
